newsitem.title: JAPAN: U.S. Treasuries steady in Tokyo, trend brightens.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries steady in Tokyo, trend brightens.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries maintained overnight gains at the Tokyo midday on Wednesday, but the topside was capped by light profit-taking, traders said.
Lower-than-expected employment cost index (ECI) data soothed market sentiment and triggered heavy short-covering in New York, they said.
Traders refrained from trading actively in Asia as they were waiting for more U.S. economic indicators scheduled this week, including April payroll data on Friday, they said.
The key 6-5/8 percent 30-year bond was unchanged from the New York close at 95-16/32, yielding 6.98 percent.
The June T-bond futures contract was unchanged from the previous close at 108-30/32.

The ECI rose 0.6 percent in the first quarter, versus market expectations of a 0.9 percent increase. In addition, durable goods in March dropped 3.0 percent, the largest falloff since August of last year.

"Operators covered their short positions aggressively after the ECI as credit-tightening fears eased slightly," a brokerage trader said. "But it's too early to determine a trend in the longer term without seeing the results of other indicators this week. Many Japanese investors are still sidelined."
